D: Lightning heads to the World Grand Prix while Mater gets mistaken for a secret agent.
P: Serve dessert when Mater eats the wasabi in Tokyo thinking it's ice cream.
S: the glitzy welcome party in Tokyo
Edamame boiled in salted water for 4 minutes, drained and tossed while hot with sesame oil, chilli flakes and flaky salt, piled into small bowls.
Mater and Lightning's race stop in Paris
Thin crêpe batter rested an hour, cooked in a buttered pan, filled with ham and gruyère, folded into quarters and crisped again, cut into triangles.
London chip shop chips with curry sauce
the final race through the streets of London

Thick-cut chips fried twice until crunchy, salted and served in paper cones with a mild chip shop curry sauce and malt vinegar. Cut 1kg washed potatoes into thick chips and dry well. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes, drain and cool, then fry at 190C for 3 minutes until crisp and golden. For the sauce, soften 1 diced onion in 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp mild curry powder and 1 tbsp plain flour, then whisk in 400ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp sultanas and 1 tsp honey. Simmer 10 minutes and blitz smooth. Salt the chips and serve with sauce and vinegar.
M: the race in the Italian seaside town of Porto Corsa
Garlic and chilli softened in olive oil, prawns and cherry tomatoes added with a splash of white wine until the prawns turn pink, tossed through spaghetti with parsley.
Luigi's Uncle Topolino in his little Italian village

Chicken thighs browned and simmered 45 minutes with tomato, olives, capsicum and rosemary until the sauce is thick, served with crusty bread. Season 8 chicken thigh pieces on the bone and brown in olive oil, skin side first, then set aside. Soften 1 sliced onion, 1 sliced red capsicum and 3 garlic cloves in the pan. Add 2 rosemary sprigs, a 400g tin crushed tomatoes and 125ml chicken stock. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 45 minutes. Stir in 80g pitted kalamata olives for the last 10 minutes. Serve with a torn crusty loaf for the sauce.
W: the wasabi Mater thinks is pistachio ice cream
Pistachio ice cream scooped into chilled bowls, scattered with crushed roasted pistachios and drizzled with honey. Wasabi optional.
K: Blood orange and lemon juice with a touch of honey syrup, topped with sparkling water over ice and garnished with orange and mint. Stir 2 tbsp honey into 2 tbsp warm water to make a quick syrup. Mix 400ml blood orange juice with the juice of 1 lemon and the honey syrup. Fill 4 wine glasses with ice and a thin orange slice each. Pour in the juice mix to half full and top with 400ml cold sparkling water. Finish with a mint sprig and serve straight away.

s.note: the glitzy welcome party in Tokyo
s.how: Boil 500g frozen edamame in salted water for 4 minutes and drain. Toss while hot with a teaspoon of sesame oil, a pinch of chilli flakes and sea salt flakes. Pile into small bowls for a fancy Tokyo party.

s.note: Mater and Lightning's race stop in Paris
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 eggs and 375ml milk and rest an hour. Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan. Fill each with ham and grated gruyere, fold into quarters and crisp again in the pan. Cut into triangles and serve hot.

m.note: the race in the Italian seaside town of Porto Corsa
m.how: Soften crushed garlic and a pinch of chilli in olive oil. Add 400g green prawns and 250g halved cherry tomatoes and a splash of white wine. Cook until the prawns turn pink. Toss through 500g spaghetti with chopped parsley.

w.note: the wasabi Mater thinks is pistachio ice cream
w.how: Scoop pistachio ice cream into chilled bowls. Scatter with crushed roasted pistachios and drizzle with a little honey. Serve straight away. Do not mistake the wasabi for it, as one tow truck learned the hard way.

d.how: Stir 2 tbsp honey into 2 tbsp warm water to make a quick syrup. Mix 400ml blood orange juice with the juice of 1 lemon and the honey syrup. Fill 4 wine glasses with ice and a thin orange slice each. Pour in the juice mix to half full and top with 400ml cold sparkling water. Finish with a mint sprig and serve straight away.
